notes: Asserts the row's full arc inside ONE opencode session and ONE turn: ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready, with the FIRST waiting episode raised by the WRITE tool (permission key `edit`) and the SECOND by the READ tool (permission key `read`). TWO DIFFERENT TOOLS is the point: the phase schema below has no tool-name field, so a recipe driving both gates through one tool (two bash commands, one writing and one reading) would pass this spec identically while proving nothing about tool class. The recipe pins `permission:{edit:{gate.txt:ask}, read:{gate.txt:ask}}` and forbids bash so only the write tool and the read tool can raise them; a re-record must confirm the two gated part rows carry different `tool` values, because this file cannot. NOT known_failing: opencode is structurally immune to #1861's named-tool-allowlist shape. Its gate reaches the daemon over the hook channel added in #1719/epic #1355 -- irrlicht's own plugin (~/.config/opencode/plugin/irrlicht.js) taps opencode's `event` bus for permission.asked / permission.replied / session.idle -- and openCodeHookPayload carries ONLY {hook_event_name, session_id}. No tool name is read at any point on that path, and state_classifier rule 0's predicate is the bare bool m.PermissionPending, so a read-only gate and a mutating gate are indistinguishable to the daemon by construction. The assert is narrow rather than per-tool-call because opencode's Permission.ask returns early and publishes nothing when every requested pattern already resolves to allow. THIS REVERSES THE SIBLING 2-19 CELL's daemon=incapable, which was assessed 2026-05-29 against the STORE and predates the hook channel. PRESESSION ADAPTER: the birth is two phases -- a transient proc-<PID> row appears first and never goes working, and the SQLite-keyed ses_ session is minted with a DIFFERENT session_id on the first prompt; every post-birth phase anchors to that real session. The two *_answered phases pin NO max_delay_ms on purpose: ReleasePermissionPromptHold drops the hold without dispatching a synthetic activity (unlike the assert side, which does), so the exit from waiting lands on the next opencode store poll and its latency has never been measured. NO CYCLE COUNT is pinned beyond the two episodes the scenario itself names as its subject. cost_nonzero is deliberately NOT asserted: this host's default is a local LM Studio model with no pricing, and every existing opencode replay golden has cum_input/output tokens but no estimated_cost_usd. model is left unpinned for record to fill from the recording.

text: Pre-session (proc-<PID>) appears in ready within 2s of the opencode TUI launching. It never goes working; it exists only so the real birth below is not mis-anchored to it.
The SQLite-keyed ses_ session is minted with a DISTINCT session_id once the first prompt lands, born ready. Every phase below anchors here.
PID bound to the ses_ session
The two-step prompt drives ready -> working on the ses_ session

MUTATING half: the write tool's call on gate.txt matches the seeded `edit: {gate.txt: ask}` rule, so Permission.ask publishes permission.asked; the hook holds SignalPermissionPrompt and rule 0 turns it into working -> waiting. This is the half 2-19 already names; it is here so ONE recording can compare the two tool classes.

A bare Enter submits the overlay's preselected `once`; Permission.reply publishes permission.replied, the hold is released, and the next store poll sees the write complete -> waiting -> working. The episode ends on the ANSWER, not on the turn. No max_delay_ms: the exit edge is poll-bound, not hook-driven.

THE ASSERTION UNDER TEST. The read tool -- which only READS -- asks under its own permission key (`read`), matches the seeded `read: {gate.txt: ask}` rule, and must produce its OWN, second waiting episode: not skipped, and not merged into the write tool's episode.
A bare Enter answers the read-only overlay; the read runs and the session returns waiting -> working on the next store poll. No max_delay_ms, for the same reason as the mutating half.
session.idle fires at true turn end -> HandleStopHook -> ready. The session does not remain waiting after the last overlay closes.
Trailing idle: the session stays ready for >=10s after the last overlay, catching a session left pinned at, or falling back to, waiting.
